items.title: Etale morphisms onto a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space are formal spectra of completions of etale algebras
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: For a McQuillan affine formal algebraic space Y, that is the formal spectrum of a weakly admissible topological algebra B, the lemma establishes an equivalence between the category of representable etale morphisms of affine formal algebraic spaces into Y and the category of topological B-algebras obtained as completions of etale B-algebras, the equivalence sending such an algebra to its formal spectrum, and deduces that every such source is McQuillan (statement lines 4441-4456). The proof first checks that the functor is well defined, because an etale algebra over B induces etale maps of the quotients and hence a representable etale morphism of formal spectra, and that the formal spectrum functor is fully faithful by an earlier statement (proof lines 4458-4466). The substance is that every representable etale morphism lies in the essential image: fixing a weak ideal of definition and base changing the morphism to the corresponding affine scheme gives an etale morphism of affine schemes, and the lift of that etale map along the quotient supplies an etale B-algebra whose quotient reproduces it (proof lines 4468-4477). One then compares this algebra with the algebras obtained from the other ideals of definition: both are etale lifts of the same etale map over the fixed quotient, and the uniqueness statement for etale lifts along a locally nilpotent ideal produces a unique isomorphism between them compatible with the identification at the fixed quotient, so that the isomorphisms are compatible as the ideal varies (proof lines 4477-4488). This identifies the given space with the formal spectrum of the completion of the constructed algebra, which completes the proof (proof lines 4488-4489). The claim is H2: after the preliminary well-definedness and full faithfulness, the argument has two genuine steps -- lifting an etale map along a quotient and gluing the resulting lifts by a uniqueness statement -- and both are displayed rather than cited away.
